There absolutely are worthwhile kids. I find that I get the most rewards from those at the top and those at the bottom of the academic spectrum. The top layer gives you a few students who are sufficiently confident and responsible to really own their learning and engage with enthusiasm. They'll take some risks and ask good questions. Likewise the kids at the bottom. Once they trust you, they open up and ask the things that they were afraid to ask because they might sound dumb. Everyone kind of thinks they're dumb and gives them rote memorization to do. If you ask them to think and make connections, they tend to engage well. The students in the middle - the average kids - are sometimes the least fun to teach. They are normal nice kids, but many of them don't care much about learning. They have full lives with plenty of sports, clubs, socializing, etc. They can't be bothered with school work unless they're outright failing and their parents are kicking their backsides. There are exceptions of course, but a roomful of average kids is sometimes the most chatty and least prepared for lessons.
